definitions.explanation: A stick of calcium carbonate or gypsum used for writing on blackboards. The standard word for classroom chalk in Japanese.

examples.japanese: ⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧チョーク⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{折|お}れて→折れる：01266_oreru⟧しまった。
⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{黒板|こくばん}→黒板：02756_kokuban⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧チョーク⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{数式|すうしき}→数式：16124_suushiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いている→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: The teacher is writing a mathematical formula on the blackboard with chalk.
My hands turned white from chalk dust.

notes:
A loanword from English "chalk." This is the standard word used in Japanese schools. Although many Japanese classrooms have shifted to whiteboards and markers, chalk and blackboards remain common, especially in public schools.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チョーク⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write with chalk
- チョーク⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{粉|こな}→粉：02766_kona⟧: chalk dust
- ⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧チョーク: colored chalk
- チョーク⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: to hold chalk
- チョーク{入|い}れ: chalk holder/case

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {白墨|はくぼく}: chalk — the Sino-Japanese term; formal and somewhat old-fashioned
- ⟦マーカー→マーカー：21828_maakaa⟧: marker — used on whiteboards, the modern alternative

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase チョーク⟦{芸|げい}→芸：19343_gei⟧ (chalk art) refers to the skill of drawing impressive diagrams or illustrations on a blackboard, valued among Japanese teachers.
